hey\! 
with all this type of campaigns (get x% back per ride/earn X amount extra on each ride) the logic is same: the row is added in the driver/company balance as soon as the driver fulfils the conditions of the campaign (eg get 10 eur on top of each ride after you have 10 finished rides, 100% acceptance rate) then row is added as soon as driver has finished 10 rides without any cancellations, 11th ride will already earn the bonus. This row will be added on that day when conditions are fulfilled and will keep on changing after every finished ride until the end of campaign period.

So if campaign period is from Monday to Sunday, driver fulfils conditions on monday, row will be added on monday and it will collect all kickback during this week on this row, it is paid out with next payout
If campaign period is a) longer than a week (payout cycle) or b) crosses Sunday midnight, balance and reporting will be a mess since the history will keep on changing until the end of the campaign

For example, if there is a kickback campaign from Wednesday to next Tuesday midnight, driver fulfils the conditions on Wednesday, 

* compensation row is added in the balance on Wednesday for 10 BYR, 
* additional bonus 50BYR is added to wednesday on Thursday
* additional bonus 50 BYR is added to Wednesday on Friday
* Driver doesnt work on Saturday and Sunday
* Payout is generated including bonus 110 BYR
* additional bonus 50 BYR is added to previous weeks Wednesday on Monday
* additional bonus 50 BYR is added to previous weeks Wednesday on Tuesday
* campaign period ends
* previous weeks balance has grown by 100 BYR by the end of campaign period compared to the payout that was calculated with Sunday midnight balance
* this additional 100 BYR will be paid out with next payout BUT payouts and any of the reports for these 2 weeks that have been included in the campaign period will not match, creating confusion

This is why we recommend strongly to keep all campaign periods sweet and short, max 1 week but in that case to match with payout cycle (Mon-Sun) 

NB\! Hopefully this problem with history changing will be fixed within Q1, then the campaign periods will be a bit more flexible

A driver could rack up a huge fares and Bolt would have to pay out (unless some specific thought was put towards how we limit this - obviously a cap is a good starting point). But for this reason alone a cash prize seems ideal. 
# There is not yet a watertight 'opt in process' for force drivers to comply with the terms and conditions. In other words, we cannot force drivers to comply with them.
# We can still proceed with the current competition provided that we are not including any obligations on drivers in our terms and conditions.
# It is unlawful to provide that driver consent to publicity cannot be withdrawn. We therefore cannot oblige drivers to get involved with any post-draw publicity. Instead, I suggest we deal with this afterwards: "Hi - you have won the prize, we are intending to give this to you at place/date and take a photo for use on our website / blog, is this OK with you?". If they say "no just give me the cash" then that is that.
# More relevant for promotions, but FYI competitions/promotions going forwards must be based on 'easy to measure' / readily identifiable entry criteria. We don't want to be put in a situation where a driver says "hey - I should have qualified, give me all of your data showing me that I didn't quality". This has apparently happened already and is a total pain to respond to from a data compliance perspective. I suggest the completion of qualifying journeys is a decent metric, ideally nothing 'time related'.
# An an aside, all such competitions are 'prize draws' and our marketing shouldn't refer to 'raffles/tickets/competitions'. If you require further guidance on this then please get in touch.

# *Introduction to particular role.* We believe that the Agency shall introduce the Applicants for a particular position in order to get the Fee. Otherwise, this will lead to a situation where the Agency refers candidates without considering carefully the job requirements and still gets the Fees - while in this case it’s our in-house team who made the effort and examined whether the candidate can be fit for other roles. Thus, in our view, this provision shall stay, Do you agree?

Obviously, for us the longer is the payment term, the better, because sometimes our Finance team may be under water with invoices.While we aim to process all the invoices within 2 weeks, sometimes it may take longer. We believe this is unreasonable, because if someone makes a technical error and pays EUR 100k instead of EUR 10k, these funds shall be returned to us. Sounds reasonable? 
# *Refund in case the Applicant leaves Bolt.* We believe that Bolt shall have the right to ask for replacement or refund in case the Applicant was hired, but leaves the business on his initiative within 12 weeks. Of course we’re interested in getting a replacement, but if that is impossible (e.g. the Agency doesn’t have any candidates fit for the role of if we find a better candidate ourselves), we believe Bolt shall get a refund. Note that we’re not asking for a full refund, the scale of the refund would differ depending on how long the referred employee worked with us (e.g. if he worked from 9 to 12 weeks we’ll only be entitled to get 50% of the Fee back). A read of the NITDA regulation evinces that the provision you had referred to acts as a yardstick for assessing when consent is freely given in instances where consent is conditional to the performance of a contract. However, it is noted that the determining factor in this case is whether the Processing Activity is necessary or excessive for the performance of the contract. Further to our assessment of the process and following advise received from the OC, the KYC verification process is a necessary step to ensuring the safety of our customers and the integrity of the investigations of law enforcement agencies in the event of road accidents. From the above, it appears that the legal basis would be a mix of both “consent” and “performance of contract”.

For completion, the OC also engaged officials of NITDA on a no-name basis to provide further clarity and they are also of the opinion that the verification process will be fundamentally instrumental to our contractual obligation to provide customers with rides.

Discussed further with [@armin.allmae|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UD5NU371C] on what to do with the request. There are two problems with our current set-up 1) hard deleting users and data is not actually something that can technically be done easily and 2) there may be potential legal backlash if we delete all the data on that business account, including who were their users and what trips did they take. A very robust example - they come in a year complaining that they didn’t add the user with specific telephone number and therefore claim that they should be refunded for such falsely charged transactions. If we would delete all the data on the Business users, then we would in no way have the opportunity to defend our position by showing that user x connected to trip y was actually added by the Business Client.

Please forward the company the following response:

You have asked to delete all the data Bolt holds on your company and on its users.  Please note that the Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business clause 2.8.1 states that Bolt processes personal data as described in Bolt’s Privacy Policy for Passengers (accessible at [https://bolt.eu/legal/privacy-for-riders/|https://bolt.eu/legal/privacy-for-riders/]). The retention terms of the data is described in clause 7 of the Privacy Policy. As a general rule, personal data will be stored as long as you have an active account. If your account is closed, personal data will be deleted (according to our retention schedule and rules), unless such data is still required to meet any legal obligation, or for accounting, dispute resolution or fraud prevention purposes.

As we had a contractual relationship, then data may be required for solving any dispute that may arise from such agreement. Deleting all the data deprives us from the opportunity to evidence the fulfilment of our obligations under the agreement in the event that any claims should arise. Therefore the data will be stored by Bolt as a data controller until the term provided by the law (limitation period for possible claims).  

Your Business Account has been deactivated, meaning that the data which we hold will and can only be used to meet legal obligations, accounting and dispute resolution purposes. We assure you, that confidentiality and security of the data is guaranteed throughout the storage period.

I don’t deem this necessary to be covered in the contracts with the employees. If it’s a local safety requirement then the legal basis may be legal obligation. But either way legitimate interest as one of the legal basis under GDPR apply when cameras are used for safety and security reasons. 

However the following must be taken into account:

# Video surveillance should be used only for the following purposes:

* Control the access to the premises and to ensure the security of the premises, including the safety of our property, information and employees. 
* To prevent and if necessary, investigate unauthorised access to secure premises and protected areas. 
* To prevent, detect and investigate theft and property damages or threats to the safety of the employees working in the premises.  

It is prohibited to use video surveillance system for any other purpose, such as to monitor the work of employees or their attendance. 

2. Positioning the cameras

The location and positioning of the video cameras has to take into account the legitimate expectations of the data subject to their privacy. Therefore monitoring is not to be expected in recreational areas, sanitary areas, changing rooms etc.

3. Retention period

All personal data processed must have a retention period. No personal data should be kept indefinitely, so a proportionate and reasoned retention time must be set for keeping this data. 

Retention period must be determined depending on the purpose why this data is being collected. 

Data can be stored for no longer than it is necessary for the purposes for which it was collected (e.g the market practice for storing this data is 30-60 days, but can be shorter or longer depending on the need). 

After the retention period, recordings must be deleted automatically (overwritten by new video footage). 

4. There should be warning signs of video surveillance in place

4.1 Position of the warning sign. 
It is obligatory to install warning signs on the premises where video surveillance is carried out. The information should be positioned in such a way that the data subject can easily recognise the circumstances of the surveillance before entering the monitored area (approximately at eye level). 

4.2 Content of the warning sign. The warning sign should provide the following information:

* Information that there is video surveillance in the area (e.g camera picture, “We have video surveillance”)
* Information of the controller (“Controller: insert information of the group company”)
* Information of where further information can be found (QR code or link to the [Global Privacy Notice on Video Surveillance|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance/]). 

(Bolt has a [global privacy notice on video surveillance |https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance]used for security purposes. It describes the purposes of data processing and the legal basis for such processing.)

5. Data protection agreement with the service provider

There must be a written contract in place when the service provider as the processor is processing personal data (video content). 

The contract is important to make sure that the processor sticks to what they’ve promised to do with the personal data, and to ensure that both parties understand their responsibilities and liabilities under data protection legislation.

* Changes were reverted in {{v10.3361.10}} and [deployed|http://core-builder.internal/Releases/release/710446] at {{2021-12-10 08:08:45 UTC}}
* The total number of affected orders per business line query:
{code:sql}SELECT /* route readonly=1 */
    o.business_line, COUNT(1)
FROM payment_order o
JOIN payment p on p.payment_order_id = o.id
JOIN payment_row cr on cr.id = p.last_payment_row_id
JOIN payment_row pr on pr.id = cr.previous_row_id
JOIN user_auth_token t on t.id = CONVERT(JSON_EXTRACT(pr.token_data, '$.user_auth_token_id'), UNSIGNED)
WHERE
    o.last_update BETWEEN '2021-12-08 10:40:48' AND '2021-12-10 08:08:45'
    AND o.type = 'balance'
    AND p.payment_method_type = 'adyen'
    AND p.state = 'cancelled'
    AND cr.type = 'cancel'
    AND cr.state = 'finished'
    AND pr.type = 'prepare'
    AND pr.amount > 0
    AND pr.state = 'finished'
    AND JSON_EXTRACT(pr.token_data, '$.user_auth_token_id') IS NOT NULL
    AND t.type IN ('3ds1', '3ds2')
GROUP BY 1;{code}

Hi Afolake, the bill essentially aims to increase the fines and sanctions payable by employers upon a breach of any of the provisions under the Act. It has been contested on several occasions that the fines and penalties under the current Act is grossly inadequate and does not align with existing commercial realities. Hence, the bill seeks to revise the applicable fines upward in this regard. In addition, the bill also aims at prohibiting the continued casualization of workers beyond a maximum period of 3 months. As a result, any casual worker engaged by the Company must be given full time employment after working for a 3 months period (howbeit, upon enactment of the Bill into law). It is noted that the bill defines *casual employment* as a “temporary employment in which an employee is guaranteed work when it is needed, and there is no expectation that there will be more work in the future.” 

A more detailed review of the specific provisions relating to the increased fine shall be done once we see that the bill has gained more traction and is being enacted.

A bug was introduced in this task: 
When an order is cancelled or discounted to the final zero price, there is no information to distinguish cancellation vs campaign discount.

So before the change, we cancelled the authorisation before customer tips were captured for the discounted ride.

After the change, we start to wait for invoicing event to make the final capture the same way we do for non-zero final amount rides.

But we didn't expect that for cancelled orders there is no invoicing event at all. So money stuck in the authorised state without cancellation called.

*17.4* - Breach of Code of Conduct shall be considered a material breach which gives the counterpart the right to terminate the agreement if breach is not remedied within 30 days of a written request to do so. This is new and was not included in the previous T&Cs. I would advice you to scan through the CoC ([https://www.axfood.com/globalassets/startsida/hallbarhet/strategi/uppforandekod-axfood-slutlig-eng.pdf|https://www.axfood.com/globalassets/startsida/hallbarhet/strategi/uppforandekod-axfood-slutlig-eng.pdf]) to get a sense of what we’re committing to. My biggest concern is our undertaking in relation to subcontractors (2nd to last section on page 3):

'The Supplier is expected to be able to show that it has done its utmost to comply with the Code of Conduct, and that its sub-suppliers, in turn, do the same. The Supplier must be aware of where there may be risks in the supply chain which could entail deviations from the Code of Conduct, and be able to state how the Supplier is working to mitigate and respond to these risks'.

My points is that I assume that we cannot speak of to which extent our subcontractors abide by the CoC. This particular subcontractor wording is pretty soft ('done its outmost' and ‘working to mitigate and respond'). In another similar case I’m working on right now the CoC is more along the lines of us ‘warranting that our subcontractors act in accordance with the CoC’. Having to abide by CoCs are something we should expect to have to do when dealing with large and mature companies. With that in mind and given that CoCs is a question in two matters which I’m involved in right now, I’d say that we need a principal commercial decision on if we are to accept CoCs and be aware of the fact that there might be parts therein regarding (I) ourselves (maybe) and regarding (II) our subcontractors (likely) which is in breach of the CoCs put in front of us. Regarding (I) it might not be that we’re in breach but rather that I for one have no way of knowing if we are fulfilling the provisions in the CoC - do we have someone working with compliance who should be included in tickets with CoCs and who can answer these questions? 

Please note that I assume that accepting a CoC would be something these companies expects their counterparts to do. 

In this particular case you can always push back and have them delete the CoC wording in the T&Cs based on the argument that this is a new addition and if it is to be included it will add substantial lead time due you having to run the CoC by legal. Please note that this is just a blame-the-lawyers charade - my assessment of the CoC is - in sum - already provided above.

Hi\!

The legal basis for recording calls would be legitimate interest (GDPR art 6 (1) f). The following conditions must be followed:

1. *Informing the caller*

The person must be informed in the beginning of the phone call of the following:

a) about the fact of recording;
b) about the purpose of recording. 

2. *Retention period*

All personal data processed must have a retention period. No personal data should be kept indefinitely, so a proportionate and reasoned retention time must be set for keeping this data. 

2.1 Retention period must be determined by the local team depending on the purpose why this data is being collected. Data can be stored for no longer than it is necessary for the purposes for which it was collected (e.g the market practice for storing this data is 1 year but can be shorter or longer depending on the need). FYI, support tickets are stored for 3 years, so the retention period could be aligned with this. 

2.2 After the retention period, call recordings must be deleted automatically. 

*3. Data processing agreement*

There must be a written contract in place when the service provider as a processor is processing personal data. 

The contract is important to make sure that the processor sticks to what they’ve promised to do with the personal data, and to ensure that both parties understand their responsibilities and liabilities under data protection legislation.

We have a problem with {{getOrderDetails}} and {{cancelOrder}} endpoints.

They receive {{order_id}} instead of {{id}} and then we use it to query the {{reseller_order}} table. If we just remove {{city_id}} there, it can cause collisions: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/rides/marketplace/reseller/main/table/ResellerOrderTable.ts#L103-L108|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/rides/marketplace/reseller/main/table/ResellerOrderTable.ts#L103-L108] as the core order table is sharded. The {{reseller_order}} table can potentially contain records with identical {{order_id}} and different {{city_id}}.

The same goes for {{cancelDelayedOrder}} and {{getFutureOrderDetails}} although the table for future rides is not sharded in the {{order}} subsystem.

So we have to create yet another set of endpoints and switch FE to use them first.

The passenger may reasonably expect that their contact details will be shared in cases where their actions cause damage to the driver’s vehicle. Therefore, under legitimate interest it is possible to disclose the information.

Relevant for Estonia: this topic is regulated in TLS (Employment Contracts Act) and TTOS (Occupational Health and Safety Act).

*Night time*: from 22:00 - til 06:00 / from 10 PM til 6 AM

*Important restriction:* if the employee works more than 3 hrs per +every+ shift or more than 1/3 of the annual working time during nighttime, they are considered to be night time employees and additional restrictions apply - their average working hours cannot be more than 8 hrs per 24 hrs. NB\! If summarised working time is applicable, the employee should get at least 11hrs rest time daily and at least 36 hrs rest time weekly. Meaning that overtime is almost forbidden for nighttime employees.

*Payroll*: The general rule is that if not agreed otherwise, a surcharge of 25% must be added to the agreed wage. If the base wage is 25% higher than national minimum (654 EUR gross x1,25), the surcharge can be included in the wage.

*Working time*: as this is done mainly during the night time and individual account of nighttime work must be held, summarised working time condition should be applied. Meaning that the employee’s working time in one week can vary (as long as the daily and weekly resting time regulations are followed). NB\! Estonia uses rolling week, not calendar week, for keeping account on working time.

*OHAS*: as a general rule, the specifics should be consulted with the health and safety officer (what are the risks, how they are mitigated, what PPE should be used etc). From legal side - the legislation doesn’t give out limits regarding how the working time should be changed if the employee works in a dangerous environment (e.g. risks for lead-acid and LiON batteries are different and they should be mitigated accordingly). As a general rule - working in a dangerous/hazardous environment is not compensated in remuneration, but as rest time.  Transportation of batteries is generally not regarded as dangerous activity, but some restrictions may apply.

*Transportation*: batteries are classified as dangerous goods* if no exception is applicable. Special training of van drivers and marking on vans could be applicable. ADR sets an exception to the general rule - further analysis is needed. If the batteries are classified as dangerous, additional training to the driver operating the van is needed. NB\! This is only applicable to removable and/or lithium batteries.

  balance_user.balance_user_booking *AS* booking

payment_allocation *AS* (

*SELECT*

  *transaction*.source_id *AS* search_token_id,

  *transaction*.source_city_id *AS* city_id,

  [http://booking.id|http://booking.id|smart-link]  *AS* booking_id,

  booking.uncovered_amount,

  *COUNT*(*DISTINCT* [bup.id|http://bup.id]) *AS* capture_count,

  *MIN*(bup.captured_ts) *AS* first_balance_capture_created,

  *MAX*(bup.captured_ts) *AS* last_balance_capture_created

*FROM*

  balance_user.balance_user_booking *AS* booking

  *LEFT* *JOIN* balance_user.balance_user_billing_transaction *AS* *transaction*

    *ON* booking.transaction_id = *transaction*.id

    *ON* allocation.booking_id = [http://booking.id|http://booking.id|smart-link] 

    *AND* allocation.is_active *IS* *TRUE*

  *LEFT* *JOIN* balance_user.balance_user_payment *AS* bup

    *ON* [bup.id|http://bup.id] = allocation.payment_id

  *LEFT* *JOIN* payment_allocation_step_one *AS* paso

    *ON* paso.search_token_id = *transaction*.source_id

    *AND* paso.city_id = *transaction*.source_city_id

    *AND* paso.booking_id = [http://booking.id|http://booking.id|smart-link] 

*WHERE*

  *transaction*.source_type = 'ride_hailing'

  *AND* paso.booking_id *IS* *NOT* *NULL*

),

payments *AS* (

*SELECT*

  [co.id|http://co.id] *AS* order_id,

  pac.booking_id,

  co.city_id,

  *COALESCE*(*MAX*([pr.id|http://pr.id]), *MAX*([pr2.id|http://pr2.id])) *AS* id

*FROM*

  company_order *AS* co

  *LEFT* *JOIN* payment_allocation *AS* pac

    *ON* pac.search_token_id = co.search_token

    *AND* pac.city_id = co.city_id

    *ON* po.order_id = *COALESCE*(pac.booking_id, [co.id|http://co.id])

    *AND* po.city_id = *COALESCE*(pac.city_id, co.city_id)

  *LEFT* *JOIN* payment_payment *AS* p

  *LEFT* *JOIN* payment_payment_row *AS* pr

    *ON* pr.payment_id = [http://p.id|http://p.id|smart-link]

    *ON* [pr2.id|http://pr2.id] = p.last_payment_row_id

*WHERE*

),

failed_initially_legacy *AS* (

payments_aggregate *AS* ( -- get the pr data for legacy flows + balance flows with pr data (will exclude balance flow transactions w/o pr data)

    *AND* co.city_id = ot.city_id

    *ON* pac.search_token_id = co.search_token

    *AND* pac.city_id = co.city_id

  *LEFT* *JOIN* payment_payment_order *AS* po

    *ON* po.order_id = *COALESCE*(pac.booking_id, [co.id|http://co.id])

    *AND* po.city_id = co.city_id

  *LEFT* *JOIN* payment_payment *AS* p

    *ON* p.payment_order_id = [po.id|http://po.id]

  *LEFT* *JOIN* payment_payment_row *AS* pr

    *ON* pr.payment_id = [http://p.id|http://p.id|smart-link] 

  *LEFT* *JOIN* payment_payment_problem *AS* ppr

The T&C for Bolt Business ([https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-business/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-business/|smart-link] ) states in clause 2.8 that _Bolt and Customer remain separate data controllers regarding any personal data processed under this Agreement._

As a controller Bolt decides the means and purposes for processing the data in order to provide the service (Bolt Business to the Customer). Bolt is the one collecting the data, registering and administering the users, providing the platform and providing the opportunity for Users (Employees) to make use of Bolt Business in the limits set by Customers. 

The fact that we are providing a service to another organisation does not necessarily mean that we would be acting as a data processor. 

The current agreement added is a data processing agreement deeming us a data processor. The data sharing in question is done between the parties in a controller-controller relationship. 

We can conclude a data sharing agreement with the client (although data sharing agreement is not obligatory under GDPR). The template can be found here: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HBIFgjhnXRAOZyX9PiX3vkRLrtl4lH8-9HNV6w8RVWo/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HBIFgjhnXRAOZyX9PiX3vkRLrtl4lH8-9HNV6w8RVWo/edit|smart-link] .

Hi [~accountid:60e96a31131bf80069e1459f] and @christian - I’m afraid the news are not really good for this one. DLA just reverted: 

* +Bolt cannot hide the elements of calculation / components of the 'tarifa' in the App+ - the law (Law 45/2018) is  adamantly clear on the elements that the platform must convey to the customer in terms of pricing:

_Article 19_ 

_1 - Without prejudice to the other obligations set out in this law, the electronic platforms must make available for each service, before the start of each journey and during the journey:_

       _b._ *_The price of the journey, the elements that compose the calculation formula and respective weighting factor_*_, under the terms of article 15._

_Article 15_

_1- TVDE service provision may be remunerated by applying one or more tariffs to the distance travelled and/or time spent in transport, or by applying a fixed price determined prior to contracting the service. (...)_

_4 -_ *_The electronic platform must make available to the user in a clear, perceptible and objective manner, before the beginning of each journey and during the same_*_:_

_a)_ *_The formula for calculating the price_*_, namely indicating in a discriminated manner_ *_the total price, the intermediation fee applied and the applicable tariffs, namely by distance, time and dynamic tariff factor_*_;_

_b)_ *_An estimate of the price of the journey to be made, calculated on the basis of the elements provided by the user and the weighting factors that make up the formula for calculating the price_* _to be charged by the operator of the service._

* +The cancellation fee must also be displayed+: it’s a matter of contracting terms and consumer defence rules make it mandatory for any service provider to disclose this type of terms.

The reason is different behaviour of Payment’s refund API for card payments and so called modern payment methods (PayPal, iDeal etc). Card payments can be refunded if payment is captured and can be cancelled if not captured yet. For modern payment methods payment should be in captured state in order to be refunded otherwise INVALID_PAYMENT exception is thrown.

Just confirmed with Payments that they have plans to implement the same behaviour for modern payment methods as for cards. ETA January 2022.

Until then we could ignore INVALID_PAYMENT exception and not fail the task.

Hi David, one more question - are we talking about two electronic complaint books registered under the same entity or are we talking about two copies of physical books registered under the same entity?

*Regarding scenario 1, there are limitations*.

For example, if a company develops two different economic activities, having two distinct CAE (“Economic Activity Classification”, which is the numerical code that frames the Portuguese economic activities by industry, in Portuguese, _Código de Atividade Económica_), even in this scenario such company can only have one registered complaint book.

In other words, there should not be a complaint book for each company`s CAE.

If there are several CAEs the company must choose the CAE corresponding to its main activity in order to determine which Regulatory or Supervisory Entity should be included in its sole complaint book.

*Regarding scenario 2, there are no limitations*.

There are no limitations on the existence of two (or more) physical copies of the same complaint book (registered under the same company).

A company can have as many physical copies of the same complaint book as establishments in which it carries out its commercial activity and where it provides services to the public (such as head offices, branches or commercial establishments, regardless of their name / identification).

3. High level goal: The lifecycle marketing team can easily download all comms performance KPIs from CleverTap
 (for each product line)

2. What is the problem?
-> Comms engagement metrics are available in Looker, but we’re missing campaign conversions so some teams (e.g. rider) are not using the Looker dashboards. Instead, they download the stats from CleverTap each month
->There are Looker views for campaign conversions, but these combine CleverTap events and service database data, which make them unreasonably resource heavy. Due to that, we have only made the conversion data available for a limited time period, which is not enough for the teams and they don’t use this data.

Current plan for solution:
-> Move the conversion queries to an ETL and use the ETL in Looker data modelling. This ETL runs once a month and adds the results for the previous month to the historical campaign performance table
-> Instead of service database data, use Segment events for calculating the conversions. Background: we send Segment events to CleverTap, so we could measure conversions in CleverTap. We can export these events to S3 alongside CleverTap system events and use them for calculating the conversions in the ETL as well.

There’s an example of what the ‘ideal world’ data output in Looker should look like (starting in cell B4): [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dYaGj5Gd_i-1vgHlF75haqkCF4_kfgI7M53D27HKV70/edit#gid=0&range=B4|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dYaGj5Gd_i-1vgHlF75haqkCF4_kfgI7M53D27HKV70/edit#gid=0&range=B4|smart-link] 

Possible scope expansion idea: should we mimic CleverTaps csv export and move sent, opened, clicked, unsubscribed metrics to the ETL as well? 
Reasons:
-> Would simplify data modelling in Looker
-> Would make the dashboards faster for end users
-> The queries already exist in Looker views, so easy to do

Why not?
-> We currently expect LCM specialists to do the data modelling for the comms performance dashboards themselves. Moving the queries from Looker to the ETL limits their capability to do so.

For driver campaign conversions, a new campaign conversions query was created.

_Hi Yaser,_

_Thank you for your email._

_Accor has asked that all supply partners (not just Bolt) whose services are available to Accor customers have what we call “Third Party Enforceable Terms” (TPET's") in their contracts with Karhoo._

_The TPET’s structure permits Accor to make a claim directly against the supply partner if (i) the supply partner fails to meet the requirements covered by the scope of the TPET's and (ii) there is a claim against Accor in relation to the same. In the present instance, an example could include Bolt not complying with its obligations of using its best endeavours to ensure that the Bolt Platform Supply provides transportation services in accordance with the law having in place all the required licences, registrations, other authorisations and insurance. The TPET structure is used as Accor has no direct contractual relationship with Bolt._

_It’s highly unlikely that Accor would need to enforce the TPET’s. This is because, contractually, Accor does not provide any services to the customer (per the Karhoo Platform T&Cs structure) and so customer claims should be directed at the drivers as opposed to Accor. There would therefore be no need for Accor to enforce the TPET’s. However, given the theoretical possibility of a customer claim against Accor, Accor’s lawyers have asked that Karhoo ensure that all supply partners have TPET’s in their contracts and have asked that the liability cap of supply partners under the TPET’s (which are already in the Bolt/Karhoo contract) be a minimum of 12 months fees which requires an increase from 3 months to 12 months for Bolt and therefore the addendum._

_In relation to your other question surrounding clause 2.2, this is an anomaly of English law. In order for an agreement to be valid, “consideration” must be given for it to be binding. Hi all, I set out below my comments and some questions to the business team. If we proceed with this contractor - please ensure that a fully completed contract is reviewed by the legal team before it is signed (if signed under the PoA) so the same template can then be used for further signings in the future. 

Annex 2 - This requires a detailed scope of duties to be provided (currently blank). This is important as this links back to the scope of liability of the Contractor - I would suggest that this is pre-populated with some generic duties that are applicable to all premises. Anything more specific to each premises can be added on an ad hoc basic. It is imperative that this is filled out. 

Why is Annex 2 referring to “security personnel’s duties” - if a typo, please remove.

Annex 2 also needs to specify the days and the times on which the cleaning takes places - to ensure this links back to Clause 8 correctly - might be best, again, to have a template placeholder to ensure this is not missed off. 



Clause 1(5) refers to services being delivered in accordance with the works schedule specified in Annex 1 - but there is no placeholder for this works schedule in Annex 1 or the other Annexes? This is important as this should detail how the contractor delivers its service. 


Annex 3 and 4 are missing from the template. Every annex should be provided, or references to them removed if not relevant. 


Clause 1(6) refers to additional services and the payment terms for such services *cannot be longer than 7 days* from the issue of the VAT invoice. Please change to 21 days - we are a global company and payment of invoices can take some time. 



Clause 2(1) - the term “Parties” is not defined. In any event it should just be the Contractor that undertakes to provide the cleaning services as referred to in Clause 2(1). 


Clause 3(1) - From a business perspective, are there any specific requirements we would like the cleaning staff to meet? E.g. any basic training etc? 


Clause 4(2) - Can we have termination on a 30 days’ notice please, the notice period to be calculated from the day after the notice is served. This would be much clearer. 


Clause 4(4) - the Contractor can terminate the contract by giving 3 day’s notice, where there has been e.g. a breach of the payment terms. Can we push back on this or first  have other safeguards before the contract is terminated for non-payment? As mentioned, being a global company payment of invoices can take some time.

If we want a reciprocal right to terminate the contract for a serious breach - business please to confirm what they see would be such material breach(es) in this context? 


Clause 5(6-11) - Suggest to remove this as Bolt should not be responsible for Contractor’s employee relationships. Agree with Weronika’s comment - best to have a contract for fixed term rather than an indefinite period. 


Clause 6(3) - payment within 21 days of invoice please (as mentioned above)


Clause 6(4) - reference to a monthly report being provided by the contractor to accompany the invoices - is the business happy to take the responsibility of accepting these reports? Current drafting states that if not rejected (with reasons given) within 2 days (does not say working days) - it will be deemed to be accepted. If the business accept this - suggest it is drafted into the contract that these reports are sent by email to named persons of the team - e.g. Pawel/Agnieszka? What happens if this report is not provided - can Bolt delay payment until this is received? 


Clause 7(3) - is this an attempt to limit the liability of the contractor, in respect of a single incident, to a month’s fees? I don’t think they should be placing such a limit at all? Can they clarify what is intended here please? 


Highlighting that Annex 5 (Clause 2, paragraphs 5 & 6) - states that the contractor *shall not be liable for any property damage if Bolt fails to notify of such damage the business day after it has been discovered AND if Bolt fails to draw up an investigation report* - this is a very short time period and also what form does this report need to be in? This is onerous and has serious consequences. 


(Some numbering in Annex 5 has gone awry\!)


Annex 5 Clause 4 (Para 6 & 8) - why do Bolt have to make a claim form to the Contractor’s insurance company? We have no contractual relationship with them. And paragraph 8 suggests that Bolt would only get paid once the Contractor is paid by its insurer. This should be removed. The Contractor needs to pay us the damages due and then recover from their insurer. 


Clause 8 provides a list of technical requirements for the premises - assume business are happy with these. 


Clause 8(7) - please remove as we do not wish to have our logo being used by the cleaning company or have our co-operation terms being shared with third parties. 


Page 7 direct marketing stuff - can we have this removed please



Our Data Protection team are reviewing Clause 9(1) and Annex/Schedule 6 and will provide their comments separately (if they have any).


Please let me know if anything is unclear.

Hi Andy, You requested a high level review via slack,  I scanned through the agreement and my comments are as follows:

*Section 1, clause 1.7 ‘Cancellation’* - Bolt has a right to cancel the assignment of any Worker, subject to Applicable Laws and the provisions of the employment agreement. As I understood from our earlier chat, we are interested in having a right to terminate without cause  giving x days notice, i.e. the termination right should not be subject to applicable law/ employment agreement. 

*Section 2, Clause 2.4b ‘Severance Deposit Fund’* - covers the costs Acumen suffers as a direct result of a breach of the Workers agreement and the breach is *at least in part* caused by Client. Bolt should only pay if the breach is caused by Bolt (direct causal link between Bolt’s breach and costs).

*Clause 3.10 Automatic renewal, no right to terminate without cause/ for convenience.* Bolt should have a right to terminate the agreement without cause giving x days prior notice.

*Section 4 Indemnity* - very broad indemnity clause, the indemnity clause of both parties should be limited (see the example in the EOR provider checklist). 

*Section 7 Non-Solicitation* - 5 years is a bit excessive. 

*Personal Data section missing* - should be added, sample in the checklist.

_(1)   General services:_

_·       complying with all applicable laws in the jurisdictions where it provides services to Client and will ensure services provided comply with applicable law;_

* _Probationary period (incl. conditions applicable to the probation period such as will any period of sickness absence or vacation extend the length of the probationary period)_

* _statutory benefits and leaves (incl. maternity leave, vacation and sick leave, health benefits)_

* _pensions_

* _termination requirements_

_·       enrolling the Professional(s) in benefits plans that meet the minimum statutory requirements in the selected jurisdiction, or, at the Client’s sole option, are in addition to the minimum requirements;_

_·       establishing payroll to pay the Professional(s)’ compensation, expense reports, and any other necessary or incidental payments;_

 

_(2)   Monthly services:_

* By producing _engaging training materials_, and
By designing _impact-driven training programs_ that grow skills and knowledge

* We plan and roll out monthly knowledge assessments (MKA’s) to ensure agents are up to date with the latest product and process updates

* Onboard Trainers, L&D teams and Solution Coaches - supporting them in training efforts for their Agents that support Bolt customers

* We create training for ad-hoc process changes and issues identified as being complex/needing training intervention
* We prepare courses on various topics to help existing Agents develop new skills

* *Agent enrolment:* 24 business hours
*New training course*: 2 - 4 weeks (this may also depend on the topic complexity, examples/data provided and available information)
*Existing training course update*: 1 - 2 weeks

*Where you can help us*

* Identifying and reporting any knowledge gaps and their perceived root causes to us 
* Escalate identified issue to our team - please do not create your own training materials or solutions - it is on our team to find the optimal solution
* Gathering and providing supporting logic for training requests (deep dive findings, ticket examples, Slack threads, etc.)

“_I would like to emphasize that my Bolt account could not have just been accessed by someone who currently has access to my old phone number. As you are well aware, you also need to enter the password to log in to the Bolt app. This means that my password has been hacked, and there has been a data breach on Bolt's side compromising my personal data saved in my account.”_ 
-- This statement is wrong. 
Bolt rider accounts don’t have usernames or passwords. You log in by entering your phone number and then Bolt sends a confirmation SMS to that number. Once the confirmation code is entered the user gets access to the account. 


There has not been a data breach and it is the customer’s fault for not notifying Bolt when their number changed.

If the customer gets a new phone number they will need to delete their old account and create a new one with the new phone number. 
When a customer ends his or her contract with their telco provider then the number becomes inactive. However, telcos give out the numbers after some time (the time can range from a few months to several years). This means that if the previous Bolt customer doesn’t contact us to get their account deleted the new account owner can log into the account because they can now receive the confirmation SMS. After logging in they can see all the usual details available in the Bolt app - name, email, rides’ history, last 4 digits of the credit card number, home and work address.
It is also important to note that when you change your phone number and SIM card it doesn’t mean that you will automatically lose access to the Bolt account associated with that number. You will stay logged into the Bolt app until you log out and you can continue ordering rides as normal. So, it is possible to use the Bolt app years after you have given up the associated phone number -- and the number might have already been given to a new customer. However, if the person stops using the account then after some period of time we automatically archive it to prevent such incidents from happening. In most countries, it is 180 days.

As pointed out earlier, it is the customer’s responsibility to notify Bolt within 7 days so we can archive the account.

As a token of good will we can refund the orders made by the new owner of the phone number

{code:sql}--PROVIDER ENHANCED SELF ORDERS
WITH related_accounts AS (
WITH providers_eater_account AS (
	SELECT DISTINCT
	dp.id AS provider_id,
	dp.email,
	dp.phone,
	u.id AS user_id,
	u.email,
	u.phone,
	ud.device_uid,
	pmu.card_alias
	FROM delivery.delivery_provider_provider AS dp
	LEFT JOIN pii.user_user AS u ON LOWER(u.email)=LOWER(dp.email) OR u.phone=dp.phone
	LEFT JOIN fraud_user_device AS ud ON ud.user_id=u.id AND ud.is_ignored=0
	LEFT JOIN payment_payment_user AS pu ON pu.external_id=u.id
	LEFT JOIN payment_payment_method_user AS pmu ON pmu.payment_user_id=pu.id
	WHERE u.created>='2021-01-01'
	AND ud.created>='2021-01-01'
	AND pu.created>='2021-01-01'
	AND pmu.created>='2021-01-01'
	),
	providers_related_eater_accounts AS (
	SELECT DISTINCT
	ud.user_id
	FROM providers_eater_account AS pea
	LEFT JOIN fraud_user_device AS ud ON ud.device_uid=pea.device_uid AND ud.is_ignored=0
	UNION 
	SELECT DISTINCT
	pu.external_id AS user_id
	FROM providers_eater_account AS pea
	LEFT JOIN payment_payment_method_user AS pmu ON pmu.card_alias=pea.card_alias
	LEFT JOIN payment_payment_user AS pu ON pmu.payment_user_id=pu.id
	)
	SELECT DISTINCT
	prea.user_id
	FROM providers_related_eater_accounts AS prea
)
SELECT
x.country,
x.order_id,
x.created,
x.payment_instrument,
x.payment_method_type,
x.delivery_type,
x.user_id,
x.provider_id,
x.price_eur,
x.collected_amount_eur,
x.total_refund_eur,
x.debt_eur,
x.payment_type,
x.bad_payment_eur,
x.provider_campaign_eur
FROM (
	  WITH price AS (
      SELECT
      city_id,
      order_user_basket_id,
      CASE WHEN POSITION('card' IN listagg(payment_method_type,','))>0 THEN 'card' WHEN POSITION('cash' IN listagg(payment_method_type,','))>0 THEN 'cash' ELSE 'bolt_credit' END  as payment_method_type,
      SUM(booked_amount) AS price
      FROM delivery.delivery_order_booking_item
      GROUP BY 1,2
      ),
      refunds AS (
      SELECT
      city_id,
      order_id,
      SUM(CASE WHEN to_agent_type='global_user' THEN sum_with_vat ELSE sum_with_vat*-1 END) AS refund
      FROM delivery.delivery_invoicing_record
      WHERE "type"='refund'
      AND (from_agent_type='global_user'
      OR to_agent_type='global_user')
      GROUP BY 1,2
      ),
      received_cash AS (
      SELECT
      order_id,
      city_id,
      SUM(COALESCE(amount,0)) AS amount
      FROM delivery.delivery_order_order_payment_info
      WHERE state IS NULL
      GROUP BY 1,2
      ),
      payment_allocation AS (
      SELECT
      booking_id,
      SUM(amount) AS amount
      FROM balance_user.balance_user_payment_allocation AS upa
      WHERE upa.is_active=TRUE
      GROUP BY 1
      ),
      provider_campaign AS (
      SELECT DISTINCT
  	  order_id,
  	  city_id,
	  sum_with_vat
	  FROM delivery.delivery_invoicing_record
	  WHERE TYPE='foodCampaign'
	  AND from_agent_type='bolt_issuer'
      ),
      payment_problem AS (
  	  SELECT
	  payment_id,
	  created,
	  state,
	  RANK () OVER (PARTITION BY payment_id ORDER BY created DESC) AS rnk
	  FROM fraud_user_payment_problem
	  WHERE state<>'ignored'
	  AND created>=DATEADD('year',-1,current_date)
	  GROUP BY 1,2,3
	  )
      SELECT DISTINCT
      o.country AS country,
      o.id AS order_id,
      o.created,
      CASE WHEN pr.price=bi.booked_amount THEN 'bolt_credit' ELSE pr.payment_method_type END AS payment_instrument,
      co.payment_method_type,
      o.type AS delivery_type,
      o.master_user_id AS user_id,
      o.provider_id,
      ROUND(COALESCE(pr.price/r.rate,0),2) AS price_eur,
      CASE WHEN payment_instrument='bolt_credit' THEN price_eur ELSE ROUND(COALESCE(pa.amount/r.rate, NULLIF(rc.amount/r.rate,0), co.allocated_amount/r.rate, 0),2) END AS collected_amount_eur,
      ROUND(COALESCE(ref.refund/r.rate,0),2) AS total_refund_eur,
      CASE WHEN payment_instrument<>'card' THEN price_eur-collected_amount_eur ELSE 0 END AS debt_eur,
      CASE WHEN co.last_payment_row_type='chargeback' THEN 'chargeback' WHEN pp.state IS NOT NULL THEN 'payment_problem' WHEN (co.last_payment_row_type='capture' AND co.last_payment_row_state='error') THEN 'failed_payment' ELSE co.last_payment_row_type||' '||co.last_payment_row_state END AS payment_type,
      CASE WHEN co.last_payment_row_type='chargeback' OR pp.state IS NOT NULL OR (co.last_payment_row_type='capture' AND co.last_payment_row_state='error') THEN ROUND(COALESCE(co.capture_amount/r.rate,0),2) ELSE 0 END AS bad_payment_eur,
      COALESCE(pc.sum_with_vat/r.rate,0) AS provider_campaign_eur
      FROM delivery.delivery_order_order as o
      JOIN delivery.delivery_order_user_basket as oub ON oub.order_id = o.id AND oub.city_id=o.city_id
      JOIN delivery.delivery_basket_user_basket_booking as ubb ON ubb.user_basket_id=oub.user_basket_id AND ubb.city_id=oub.city_id AND ubb.state IN ('succeeded','timed_out')
      JOIN balance_user.balance_user_billing_transaction AS bt ON bt.source_id=ubb.id AND ubb.city_id=bt.source_city_id
	  JOIN balance_user.balance_user_booking as bub ON bub.transaction_id=bt.id
      LEFT JOIN price AS pr ON pr.city_id=oub.city_id AND pr.order_user_basket_id=oub.id
      LEFT JOIN refunds as ref ON ref.order_id=o.id AND ref.city_id=o.city_id
      LEFT JOIN payment_allocation AS pa ON pa.booking_id=bub.id
      LEFT JOIN received_cash AS rc ON rc.order_id=o.id AND rc.city_id=o.city_id
      LEFT JOIN provider_campaign AS pc ON pc.order_id=o.id AND pc.city_id=o.city_id
      LEFT JOIN vw_currency_exchange_rates as r ON DATE(r.valid_on)=DATE(o.created) AND r.currency=o.currency
      LEFT JOIN delivery.delivery_order_booking_item as bi ON bi.order_user_basket_id=oub.id AND bi.city_id=oub.city_id AND bi.payment_method_type='bolt_credit'
      LEFT JOIN commerce.orders AS co ON co.city_id=o.city_id AND co.order_id=o.id AND co.order_type='food_delivery' AND co.payment_method_group IS NOT NULL AND co.booking_id=bub.id
      LEFT JOIN payment_problem AS pp ON pp.payment_id=co.max_payment_id AND pp.rnk=1
      WHERE o.state='delivered'
      AND o.created>='2021-09-01'
      --AND (provider_campaign_eur>0
      --OR bad_payment_eur>0
      --OR total_refund_eur>0
      --OR debt_eur>0)
      ) AS x
      JOIN related_accounts AS y ON y.user_id = x.user_id{code}

The stateful stuff is tricky to run in multiple regions simultaneosly, unless it is designed to run that way. It’s not only mysql databases, there are other stateful components that we don’t know yet how to run there.

Namely, [SQS/SNS|https://github.com/bolteu/terraform-sns-sqs] that is crucial part of communication between microservices, it is used in all asynchronous workflows. We know that SNS is able to push messages to queue in different region, so we could send duplicate events to another region. But backend would have to handle this correctly.

Also [redis master/slave setup|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/2656896546/Redis], which is designed to run in single low latency location and single AZ failure. Correct solution seems to have independent redis setup in each region and duplicate writes.

Another issue is [elasticsearch|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/2656732624/Elasticsearch], the free version we are running does not have cross site replication feature. When adding single node that has higher latency, it will reduce write performance for indexes that are on it. Therefore it also requires independent clusters in each region. Alternative is to switch to paid version, with cross cluster replication it can replicate to another cluster for disaster recovery, but does not support active-active for writes.


We also have S3 buckets and Kafka setup, that are single region based.

In conclusion, we need to include some seasoned backend engineers to understand how to enable multi region for stateful services, and look it service by service.

[~accountid:5d91b1930c2a5d0dd87aad89] If the new index is only for deletion, this is a very inefficient approach. Reasons are as follows:

# Adding a new index is an expansive cost operation for huge and many tables.
# Insert, update cost will be increased after adding a new index.
# Retrieving the target rows may be fast but the delete query becomes more expansive due to a new index.
# Obsoleting the index after use will be another operation cost. 

Therefore I recommend the following approach.

Use the PK column to scan the data and delete the row if the condition matches:



{noformat}const query = sql`DELETE
                FROM ${TableId.orderPriceNegotiationEvent}
                WHERE id >= ${var} and id < (${var} + ${limit})
                  AND state = ${PriceNegotiationEventState.SENT}
                  AND created < FROM_UNIXTIME(${createdBeforeTs})`
                ;
var = var + limit;{noformat}

Something else to consider, around credentials management.

We might want to use AWS Secrets Manager, which seems promising but has some caveats. 

I have been discussing this with (the awesome\!) [@andrus.viik|https://taxify.slack.com/team/UM4TDL282].
Here's the deal.
DS [users|https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/home#/users/FrancescoPochetti] inherit from the [SageMakerUsers|https://console.aws.amazon.com/iamv2/home#/groups/details/SageMakerUsers?section=users] Group with AmazonSageMakerFullAccess policy prefixed with {{AmazonSageMaker-}}


{noformat}{
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
                "secretsmanager:DescribeSecret",
                "secretsmanager:GetSecretValue",
                "secretsmanager:CreateSecret"
            ],
            "Resource": [
                "arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:AmazonSageMaker-*"
            ]
        },{noformat}

This means we can create and consume Secrets as long as they are prefixed with {{AmazonSageMaker-}}
It also means that I can read [~accountid:5c6bbd9d00a665752ca2c9e8] 's [Github|https://eu-central-1.console.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/home?region=eu-central-1#!/secret?name=AmazonSageMaker-siim-github] Secret, for instance, which somehow goes against the principle of "secrecy", but it is the consequence of the policy.

A potential solution would be to have a personal policy attached to each user, e.g. something like this

{noformat}"Resource": [
                "arn:aws:secretsmanager:*:*:secret:FrancescoPochetti-*"
            ]{noformat}

In this case, I'd be the only one capable of creating and consuming Secrets with that prefix.

The problems start when we add IAM Roles to the mix.
Pretty much all of DS use this [role|https://console.aws.amazon.com/iam/home#/roles/AmazonSageMaker-ExecutionRole-20180822T171180] to create and consume resources. SM Notebooks and Studio being examples of those.
So, let's say I spin up a SM Notebook using this role.
In order to read my secrets, SREs will have to add permissions to the role to read those secrets.

Roles are not tied to users, so anybody creating Notebooks with that same role would be able to consume my secrets.
They still wouldn't be able to read them from, say, the [AWS Console|https://eu-central-1.console.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/home?region=eu-central-1#!/listSecrets/]. Just from within resources created with that role.

That's far from being "bullet-proof-secret" as one would imagine.
Still way better than ENV variables, considering that they are stored in plain text somewhere to load them.
But not completely secure just yet.

Dear …

Thank you for the request. Bolt recognises the legitimate interests in making necessary and proportionate disclosures to the police and law enforcement agencies in order for the authorities to undertake statutory law enforcement functions. Bolt usually relies on the UK GDPR legitimate interest lawful basis in order to facilitate such disclosures.

The data being sought is for all the passengers who booked a cab on 11/12/2021 between 00:00 and 05:00 hours in the morning. 

You have stated that the driver in question may have dropped someone relating to a linked series of burglaries that night. 

As a controller of the data, we have to make sure that there exists a legitimate interest for the disclosure of the data. For that we need to assess the purposefulness, necessity and conduct the balancing test between the data subject interests and the legitimate interest of the third party. 

Please note that a large amount of passengers fall into the time scope provided. It is not proportionate to disclose large amount of personal data on data subjects on the fact that someone who may have booked Bolt may have been connected to the burglaries. The request does not specify any other personal identifier, including the area of the burglaries or pick up and drop off locations.  

Therefore, on the balancing test, individual’s legitimate interests, and the right of privacy, override the legitimate interests of the police request.

Failing to satisfy a legitimate interests assessment, Bolt is prohibited by law from complying with the request. There is no alternative legal basis at this time available in order to permit a lawful disclosure.

* The Seed ID is the one which is assigned to the user when the profile is qualified for the campaign 

*Explanation of the formula:* 

We Add the CleverTap ID and Seed ID then take the mode value of the same with 100 and then if the remainder is less than the control group then it is in the control group. 

Example: If the campaign control group is 20% and the CleverTap ID is 1000, when the user was qualified in the campaign the seed ID was 214, then the mod value is: (1000+214)%100 = 14. This user would be in the control group.

This issue has been not observed any longer. Closing as verified.

On 21st of December Ukrainian McDonalds ordered at least 32 rides at approximately same time. 

Just before doing these rides, their balance was just below their credit limit.

Business-invoicing threw out the errors about {{insufficient funds}}

!image-20211223-121458.png|width=1657,height=573!


 ) but that didn’t prevent the balance to go much below credit limit. 



So as a result balance finished up being -31000UAH while credit limit was set to 20000UAH.

Based on the above, we can logically deduce that:

* {{INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE}} error is thrown only in one place, and this is {{internal/getPreparedPayment}} endpoint which leads to {{validateClaim}} method. The error comes from here. Only here the credit limit is checked
* Credit limit is *not* checked when new claim is created
* {{internal/getPreparedPayment -> validateClaim}} is called after claim is already created and exists in DB, presumably by the end of the order → it is too late to check if the limit is exceeded or no by that time

What I think happened was just a bad coincidence. There were a lot of rides ordered at approximately same time, just before the credit limit was reached. Since credit limit validation happened only after order was already in progress/finished (not sure about it), some of these orders finished which caused credit limit to be exceeded by 50%.  

That means that our credit limit logic is flawed. 

Proposed solution:

We should move the logic of checking credit limit for PP companies to {{internal/preparePayment}} endpoint, which in fact is {{createClaim}} method. This is the right place to check if the order can be made or no. If limit is already exceeded, we shouldn’t even allow to create a claim.

 And remove the logic from {{internal/getPreparedPayment}} ← this endpoint should only retrieve already prepared payment. There should be no logic of checking whether the ride can be made or no - the ride already happened.

In order to operate under the Brussels *temporary derogation regime*, BOLT electronic platform has to be approved by the Brussels Minister-President. In order to obtain this approval, BOLT has to prove that :

* It has an establishment unit in Belgium;

* It provides for taxi booking services to the public;

* Its allows Brussels transport administration (Bruxelles Mobilité) to have access to the following up to date information:

§  the identification data of operators and drivers registered on the platform

§  the general terms and conditions of membership of the platform applicable to operators and drivers, which may neither prohibit them from also joining other platforms of their choice nor impose additional costs on those who join several platforms

§  the platform's general terms of use applicable to customers.

The documents evidencing that the above requirements are met shall be sent to the Brussels Minister-President who has then a period of 10 days to take a decision.

The reason for this behaviour is - on the app start we are not waiting for GPS data to be properly updated, but are using cached last known coordinate for it, and use it for calling {{getAppStateOnStartup}} which determines the product app should open on the launch. Because last known location was in Tallin, {{getAppStateOnStartup}} responds with carsharing being available, and asks app to switch to it. But on the carsharing screen, we are getting errors for any data related to carsharing (because at this time GPS is already providing an actual device location to the app, and app uses it for all the requests being sent to backend). And for some reason, app doesn’t handle this situation well. Possible behaviours for the app could be:

# Automatically switch to the available product screen
# Notify user about carsharing being unavailable, and provide user a way to manually switch to available product (as we do in micromobility)

!image-20211227-130557.png|width=1099,height=211!

Mark,

we have discussed this topic/issue a few times already I think - but never documented it properly. So it it goes:

My understanding of the current process: 

* from pay-in POV we treat all Bolt users across all Bolt verticals as a single cohort - Bolt users who pay/fail to pay for Bolt services
* such an approach is at odds with legal/contractual set- up and sometimes invites attention/questioning from users

So what’s the legal angle on this approach:

* Bolt users conclude a bunch of separate contracts with Bolt: 1 per each service (rides, rentals (x1 for scooter + x1 for Drive); food)
* Contracts may even be with different Bolt entities. Though as of 1 JAN 2022 this is lesser of an issue now that BO is taking over the RH platform operator’s role from BT. However, challenges still persist with all localised businesses (both on food and rides where the local sub is serving as an operator and Bolt’s contracting entity)
* These separate contracts for Bolt services though interrelated and cover overlapping cohorts of Bolt users - are not fully linked in the sense that a branch of one of the contracts affects rights under another one. The same is true for payments: failure to pay under one contract (e.g. rides) does not have an auto effect on payment obligations under the other contract (e.g. food).
* 

All in all:

* If the user fails to pay for Rides. We do not really have a bullet-proof legal ground to charge her failed portion when she orders on food. 
** This is a non-intense risk where Bolt Ops is an operator of all Platforms and a more intense risk where the local subsidiary is involved
** This is most likely to cause issues not directly vis-a-vis users (user raising a claim or going after us directly) but most likely by user challenging a charge of his CC/DC → and Bolt incurring a chargeback due to lack of proper legal mandate to actually make a charge (or worse - by a more general action from CC-scheme/PSP partners if this is spotted as the recurring issue with Bolt charges).

So what to do:

* Adding this lack of mandate to charge across different business verticals - > to a list of changes we need to implement to all our User T&Cs globally. Once done - the issue will be solved
* In the meantime: pls keep an eye on this issue and its manifestations through our user interactions and interactions with PSPs. If intensifies - will prioritise this change to T&Cs.



Hope this is useful.



J.

Hi,  

If a driver’s app payment from the balance page is showing 0 for a particular date then the agent should check the driver’s orders for that day and check if some trips are marked as fraudulent.

The way to connect the app payment to the trips is for the agent to check the driver’s orders for that day or range of days. The agent cannot use the app payment ID to check for the orders because app payment on the driver’s balance is for all the trips completed that particular day. From the screenshot of the driver’s balance I sent, you will notice that there is only one app payment for each day because all the driver’s card payments + bonuses for that particular day are added to give the app payment that displays on the driver's balance.

The driver will notice that their app payments in their earnings/ balance view on their driver app have disappeared or reduced for that particular day or period. At the backend, this means that the orders the driver did have been marked as fraudulent so the rider’s discounts(bonuses) that the driver was supposed to get as app payments have been removed.

Do let me know if you need any other information.

Firstly responses on the clauses Zürich wants to remove from Bolt Business T&C, 

and then my thoughts on the use of external counsel for Bolt Business matters overall, cc [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897] 

* 4.2 - ok to remove
* 4.9-4.14 - ok to remove if the Customer is on postpaid
* 4.20 ok to remove, as long as the 30 days is indicated in the agreement
* 4.21 - I would not remove. It’s elementary that the Customer would cover this cost as it’s the Customer who fully controls whether it pays up its fees in due time. In practice we haven’t applied this a lot because fortunately the ratio of debting Customers has been low. But Nick has been clear that we want this legal basis should debt issue start increasing.
* 4.22 ok to remove if its crucial for Zürich - essentially the difference from the exchange rates is marginal, so.
* 5.1 - we need to keep. This is for differentiating Bolt as the platform operator from the transportation service provision.
* 5.3 - I would not waive just like that. Would they instead be ok with the following: _“The liability of Bolt in connection with any loss or damage that Customer may incur as a result of using Bolt Business shall be equal to the actual amount received by Bolt from the Customer under the Agreement in 3 months preceding the date on which the claim arose”?_
* 5.5 - ok to remove. It doesn’t provide material additional value on top of other terms already included.


*Now in terms of external counsel usage then,*

* I suggest for the ongoing two matters where you have already reached out to SPASS (i.e Zürich and Leroy Merlin) you also finish with SPASS. _As always make sure the fees are fixed in advance as far as possible (or at least foreseeable) and make sense in terms of expected ROI from these deals. I remain available as with Zürich._
* Going forward as suggested by [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] we run with DLA. It also make sense as they were the ones who validated our new Business T&C effective from Jan 1st. *However, I don’t see overly many use cases where we actually need to reach out to external counsels on Bolt Business matters, as:*

(a) confirmed by DLA itself our new T&C is a good fit for PT _as is_,

(b) it’s such a lean offering, and we have so much knowledge already in-house how to meet the wildest Customer needs that any external can hardly provide any real value for reasonable money _- contracting playbooks in the making, dedicated special terms templates for moving fast track with Customers who bring their own corporate contracts to their table, etc,_ 

(c) with our internal Legal team ramping up we won’t be facing such bandwidth issues as we’ve done earlier. 

*Still, one problem remains for the time being, i.e afaik we won’t be having Portuguese speaking lawyers in-house for the foreseeable future. Hence we might need some help drafting*, but let’s take it case by case. I have several ideas how to streamline it w/o making external counsel cost each time. 

*So for the the time being* [~accountid:5fa511639e35e50068b366f0] please raise all transactional matters via Legal SD, and we’ll find the optimal solution. _In January I remain in the lead, likely in February_ [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] _will start taking over transactional support. Услуги «диспетчера такси», которые Bolt оказывает автомобильным перевозчикам – юридическим лицам по общему правилу облагаются в Республике Беларусь налогом на доходы иностранных организаций (*налог на доходы*) по ставке 15% (п. 1.12 ст. 189, п. 1.5 ст. 192 НК). Автомобильный перевозчик, как налоговый агент Bolt, обязан исчислить налог на доходы из вознаграждения Bolt и перечислить его в бюджет.
Вместе с тем Bolt вправе воспользоваться положениями Соглашения между Республикой Беларусь и Эстонской Республикой об избежании двойного налогообложения и предотвращении уклонения от уплаты налогов на доходы от 21.01.1997 (*Соглашение*) и получить освобождение вознаграждения Bolt от налога на доходы при условии предоставления в налоговый орган и/или перевозчикам – налоговым агентам справки налогового резидентства Bolt в Эстонии.
Для применения Соглашения Bolt предоставил перевозчикам и разместил на своем сайте справку налогового резидентства Bolt в Эстонии и его нотариально заверенный перевод на русский язык. Cогласно абз. 4 п. 2 Инструкции о порядке представления подтверждения постоянного местонахождения иностранной организации, международной организации, утвержденной постановлением МНС Республики Беларусь от 03.01.2019 № 2 «Об исчислении и уплате налогов, сборов (пошлин), иных платежей», перевозчики вправе представлять в налоговый орган скан такой справки налогового резидентства Bolt для освобождения вознаграждения Bolt от налога на доходы в соответствии с Соглашением.

As a general rule, tax on income of foreign companies (income tax) of 15% is levied on the “taxi dispatcher” services provided by Bolt to Fleet Partners - legal entities (clause 1.12 of article 189, clause 1.5 of article 192 of the Tax Code). The Fleet Partner, as a tax agent of Bolt, must calculate income tax from Bolt fees and transfer it to the budget. However, Bolt has the right to make use of the provisions of the Agreement between the Republic of Belarus and the Republic of Estonia on the avoidance of double taxation and prevention of tax evasion on income dated 21.01.1997 (*Agreement*) and get exemption from income tax on Bolt fees, provided that the tax authority and / or Fleet Partners - tax agents provide a certificate of Bolt’s tax residency in Estonia with a notarised translation into Russian. According to par. 4 clause 2 of the Instruction on the procedure for submitting confirmation of the permanent location of a company approved by the Resolution of the Ministry of Taxes and Duties of the Republic of Belarus dated 03.01.2019 No. 2 "On the calculation and payment of taxes, duties and other payments", Fleet Partners can submit a scan of Bolt’s tax residency certificate to the tax authority to exempt Bolt fees from income tax in accordance with the Agreement.

Hey Michal,

We have double-checked and yes, this is exactly how the RH process should work at the moment. If the payment method is Bolt Balance, then no blocking should take place. Marking such payments as fraud is disabled and an unnecessary step. 

Some additional context from our fraud team:

_If the unknown charge is related to a stolen card, the person would go to the bank to block it and we would get notification from the issuer regardless. So, basically, marking the payment internally, it’s just a way to flag the payment faster, it’s like an early notice of chargeback. If it’s friendly fraud (user trying to get a refund), they won’t go to the bank always and marking doesn’t help us much anyway. Therefore, no need to worry about taking an action. If payment is indeed bad, we’ll get a notification from the bank, and the payment problem will be added automatically._

App calls {{/client-commerce-proxy/user/getPaymentsDataV2}} to fetch payment templates. Apps pass the country & lat/lng to this request which can be used to get the “payment country”. Basically, even if the user’s GPS location is outside of Hungary but the pick-up location for the ride is in Hungary, the work profile payment tab won’t show. Similary, if a user with GPS location in Hungary is booking a ride in some other country, the work profile payment tab will show for them.

There are also a few other APIs that we might have to update for backward compatibility with old app versions like {{/client-commerce-proxy/user/getPaymentsData}} & {{/user/user/getPaymentMethodsPerTemplate}}.

Then we can also discard the {{user_billing_profile_id}} field in order creation API flow if ride location is Hungary to guard against any direct API calls by the user.

I prepared a short summary of the process here (see screenshot).

!Screenshot 2022-01-03 at 18.37.13.png|width=1145,height=299!

The screenshotted process is based on the consultancy of two separate entities - one being an architect, the other one being a store owner himself. 

Interestingly, our sanitary consultant bluntly said that he doesn’t know because no-one follows it and it's a “dead regulation”.

Now, to answer your question - 2 out of 3 buildings had the defined “Plan miejscowy” (“Local plan”) - meaning we can apply for the compliance certificate right away and, after up to 30 days, we can submit the change of usage request.

With the third one, it sadly doesn’t have the “Local plan” defined. In that case we requested the “Development conditions” documentation (which is a hefty book of architectural docs, according to the consultant), and only after we get it, we can apply for the compliance certificate.

According to what we know, *only after receiving the compliance certificate we can correctly submit the change of usage request*.

So it isn’t necessarily dependant on the local authorities but on the building’s documentation.

Important note is that we can check if the building has the local plan before we sign it. Discarding all the buildings without it would be an operational cost for us though.

Hey everyone,

While reviewing the comments left by Henriko and Darina on the [article draft|https://docs.google.com/document/d/111X2rAdETWuFiJB4Kejm-CF2tSD6AvMBIMb7DJcqRC4/edit], I noticed a few concerning points that I wanted to highlight and discuss with all of you. 

*To recap about the problem we’re trying to tackle* with this process update:

|Main objectives of the process update|* Raising awareness that we monitor the cleanliness state of our vehicles
* And educating users about reporting issues with the vehicle’s hygiene right away|
|What we know|* Some users leave the vehicles dirty, and some users report dirty vehicles
* Even if we call previous users, there really isn’t a way of proving which user was at fault (since none of the  users contacted so far had admitted they were the ones who left the car dirty)|
|What we need|* An efficient/feasible way to educate the users who had used a vehicle that was later reported being dirty 
* A way to see the repeat offenders (users who were discovered to frequently have used vehicles who were later reported being dirty)
* A way to prevent users from abusing the system by reporting the vehicle being dirty (even though they were the ones who made it dirty) at the end of their own ride|
|What the proposed process update includes ([article draft|https://docs.google.com/document/d/111X2rAdETWuFiJB4Kejm-CF2tSD6AvMBIMb7DJcqRC4/edit])|* Calling not the last, but the previous user to ask about the vehicle condition
** If the user says everything was fine, call the user who rented the vehicle before them
* Educate the user about reporting an unhygienic vehicle via the _Report issue_ button in the app
* Add a comment on the order page in Admin V2 with the issue description and that the user was contacted|

Since we already have [a KB article|https://support.taxify.eu/hc/en-us/articles/360021416400--User-reports-bad-vehicle-condition] for our agents - _just not an ideal one yet_ - I wouldn’t want us to rush to a decision, especially when there’s a potential growth of outbound contact involved. According to another past research project described in the [Outgoing Tickets Reduction|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CM/pages/1765343387/Outgoing+Tickets+Reduction] Confluence page, KB processes related to behavioural complaints generate the most outbound contact.

Therefore, I wanted to raise the following questions just to make sure we’ve reviewed the options thoroughly:

# Do we have any data on how much outbound contact is made to users after which the vehicle was reported dirty? (I’ve seen some requests on #transcom-bolt_carsharing_ee)
# Do we have data that confirms that creating such outbound contact (calling the user(s) or sending an in-app message in case of no response) will have a positive effect on the cleanliness state of our vehicles?
# Have we considered automating such follow-up contact with the purpose to educate the customer? Is there data that suggests this wouldn’t be a suitable solution?
# If we proceed with calling the users and adding comments manually in Zendesk as a temporary solution to gather data, do we have any other solutions in mind against which we’ll evaluate that data? Meaning, is this a temporary solution for a better solution that’s on the roadmap?

Content-wise, we can also proceed with the process update as per the [article draft|https://docs.google.com/document/d/111X2rAdETWuFiJB4Kejm-CF2tSD6AvMBIMb7DJcqRC4/edit] if we agree on this - with just a few things to keep in mind:

* We cannot assume that the user we’re calling was really at fault - therefore the comments must represent this clearly
* We have to craft the message very carefully because we might be calling users who weren’t at fault (Darina, let’s discuss and create it together after we’ve all aligned here)
* I’d suggest not to implement any logic for blocking or fining the repeat offenders yet (we have no data that would support either decision)

Sorry about the lengthy message - the dirty vehicles are a tricky issue to tackle, but I’m sure we’ll align on a great solution together 🙂
