Kas Teenuseosutaja on meie poole pöördunud juba taotlusega andmete väljastamiseks? 

Bolt Drive TC p 8 kohaselt on kasutaja kohustatud tasuma leppetrahvid mis on tulenenud temapoolsest kasutamisest. Olukorras, kus kasutaja oma kohustust kolmanda osapoole ees ei ole täitnud, tekib neil ilmselgelt ka õigustatud huvi lepingupoole andmete välja nõudmiseks. Ainus õiguslik alus, millele siin tugineda andmete väljastamiseks olekski õigustatud huvi (GDPR art 6 lg 1 p f). 

Antud olukorras tundub õigustatud huvi olemas olevat kuna parkimise korraldaja ja sõiduki kasutaja vahel on sõlmitud parkimisleping, milles on kokku lepitud leppetrahvinõudes ja seda on rikutud. Rikkumise järgselt on leppetrahvinõue esitatud kasutajale ning see on täitmata. Leppetrahvinõude täitmiseks ei ole hetkel muud alternatiivi kui kasutaja andmete edastamine kolmandale osapoolele (teenuseosutajale). Arvestades, et kasutaja võtab endale kohustuse selliseid nõudeid täita, siis võib kasutaja ka andmete edastamist teenuseosutajale mõistlikult oodata. Andmete edastamine on ainus viis eesmärgi saavutamiseks ehk kolmanda osapoole nõude täitmise tagamiseks (võid mind parandada kui siin esineb ikkagi mõni muu viis?). 

Enne andmete edastamist peaks siiski teenuseosutaja enda õigustatud huvi põhjendama, et meil oleks võimalik selle alusel andmete väljastamise üle otsustada ning see dokumenteerida. 

Sellest tulenevalt ma soovitaks Teenuseosutajal edastada meile taotlus andmete väljastamiseks koos põhjendusega õigustatud huvi olemasolu kaalumiseks ning otsuse dokumenteerimiseks GDPR art 6 lg 1 p f alusel.

Hey [~accountid:5cd9daa0bc70090d6ce26227] and [~accountid:61445ecbe057c6006a5163cc], to sum up:

If the premises are used with the new “purpose” before the expiry of the 30 day time period - there is a risk of a fine and committing an offence (as detailed in previous comments) – according to the jurisprudence such situation is similar to the change of use of the premises without *_any_* notification.

Before the expiry of 30 day time period the construction authority (Polish: _organ administracji budowlanej)_ is entitled to issue a certificate confirming that there are no grounds for raising the objection - the issuance of the certificate excludes the possibility of raising the objection by the authority and entitle the investor to change the way in which the premises is used. 

Please note that generally the authority has 1 month to issue a certificate of compliance with the local plan/compliance with the development conditions. According to the externals' experience the authorities usually issue the certificates within that period – they have confirmed that additionally by phone with one of the authorities. 

This is the legal position. I would be reluctant to take the advice of architects/store owners/sanitary consultants on an informal basis - as the consequences are very serious. Please take into account the legal risks and proceed accordingly. 

Please let me know if there are any further queries. 

Best, 

Liisa

Hi Olatunde,

For Carsharing line of business, we have long-term orders which means the user can be renting a car for days, months, and so on. As we capture payment only after the order is finished, there is a high risk that the user might not have sufficient funds after renting a car for a month (as it will cost them 1k+ EUR). In order to prevent unpaid orders, our system captures payment for long-term orders every 24h or every 50 EUR (in some cases the price might reach 50 EUR before 24h as it depends on the car model and distance). If our system has failed to capture the payment and the order is still ongoing, our CS team gets a notification about failed payment and is required to call the customer to ask them to top up their bank account. Depending on the outcome, the user either will continue his long-term order or the CS team will block the vehicle’s engine until the user adds money to their card and the payment is successful.

If we will not contact the user after having a failed payment alert - it might happen that they continue using our car for as much time as they wish and never pay for it. To answer your second question, the reminder in the app is not sufficient because in case the balance is not topped up, there is a manual action required - blocking the engine or sometimes event manually finishing the order.

We believe this debt collection is not the Customer Support responsibility, and, therefore, ask the help from commerce to find out a more scalable solution. 

In December, CS has followed up on 843 failed payments alerts which required 1 Full-Time Employee for this task. The carsharing line of business is going to enter 3 more markets as of March and many more as of May. This means, if we will not somehow automate this process or reduce volume - CS would need to handle x10 more alerts on a monthly basis.

We understand that in some cases we might still require to contact the customer as CS, however, maybe we can automate it somehow. For example, start with notification after failed payment that will inform the customer that they need to top up their balance within x period of time, retry payment automatically in x period of time after notification, and only send work for CS after 2nd unsuccessful charging attempt or similar.

Please let me know if any other clarification is needed.

* Previous approach with whole topology in {{host_az}} table only works for simple master->slave topologies. If an intermediate slave is used (M->IS->S) then new slave S can not figure top level master M (it only sees IS) and thus can not insert/update its own record in M's {{host_az}}.
* Due to above, changed the approach so that each mysql node’s {{host_az}} table only needs it's own entry. When creating a new slave, rather than try to populate {{host_az}} in the master, it will turn off binlog and update local {{host_az}} table.
* Thus,{{host_az}} table will be different in each host and will only have that host’s entry (rather then whole topology). Other entries in the table are harmless (eg: existing ones from previous work in this ticket) and will be ignored by Orchestrator. 
* Adjusted code and tested with inactive cluster (created au-d4.sqldb test slave from intermediate au-d2). Test results were OK.
* Commit and pushed code to git

(

scooter_users as (

from rental.rental_order_order o 
where state='finished' and created>'2021-01-01'
group by 1,2
),
food_users as (
select 
master_user_id as user_id,
city_id,
count(*) food_orders
from delivery.delivery_order_order  
where state='delivered' and created>'2021-01-01'
group by 1,2
)
select 
	c.name as city_name,
	ct.name as country_name,
	count(distinct case when rh_orders>0 then user_id else null end) count_of_users_with_rh_orders,
	count(distinct case when scooter_orders>0 then user_id else null end) count_of_users_with_scooter_orders,
	count(distinct case when food_orders>0 then user_id else null end) count_of_users_with_food_orders,
	count(distinct case when food_orders>0 or rh_orders>0 or scooter_orders>0 then user_id else null end) count_of_users_with_any_orders
from (	
select 
	GREATEST(rh.city_id,sc.city_id,f.city_id) city_id,

	rh_orders,
	scooter_orders,
	food_orders
from rh_users rh
full outer join scooter_users sc on rh.user_id=sc.user_id and rh.city_id=sc.city_id
full outer join food_users f on rh.user_id=f.user_id and rh.city_id=f.city_id
) t 
join admin_system_city c on t.city_id=c.id
join admin_system_country ct on c.country_code=ct.code
group by 1,2
order by 6 desc{noformat}

Sorry for the long response. AZ regulations in respect of lotteries are quite complex indeed. 
This promotion will qualify as a lottery and requires permission from the Central Bank. 
We need to provide the Central Bank the following: 
- notice of intention to hold a promotional lottery; 
- terms of the lottery;
- example of lottery ticket (can be in digital format); 
- documents in respect of the entity conducting the lottery - registration certificate, tax certificate.

Further, the lottery must be compliant with AZ laws and our App or website will need to be adjusted so that: 
- Bolt notifies users about the lottery; 
- Bolt asks the user’s consent to participate in the lottery; 
- Bolt asks users to confirm that they are over 18. 

Moreover, advertising of a promotional lottery shall provide all the main info about it (conditions, time, duration, prize, place, time and conditions of prize collection, information about lottery organiser).
